premise.claim: Issue #481 / PR body: stateful RoleInstanceSet reconciles sweep the global health observations and early-rollback signals on every request — pruneInstanceHealth performs a full Range over the global maps with one informer lister Get per entry, O(number of tracked unhealthy instances) on every reconcile.
premise.reportedComponent: pkg/reconciler/roleinstanceset/statefulmode pruneInstanceHealth (called at the top of Reconcile)
premise.patchedComponent: same function/file; throttle added around the existing sweep
premise.evidence: On base 56c4953 the counting-indexer canary TestV501PremiseBaseScansOnEveryReconcile PASSES: 3 consecutive prune calls over 2 sets x (1 unhealthy timer + 1 rollback signal) perform 12 lister reads — one full sweep per reconcile with no time-based skip (results/base-premise.txt). Per-reconcile cost on base: 9.4us @ 100 entries, 1.19ms / 960KB / 30,000 allocs @ 10,000 entries (every reconcile). On head the same map sizes cost 15ns / 0 allocs on the throttled path.

findings.claim: First prune call sweeps; calls within instanceHealthPruneInterval perform zero informer lookups; the first call at/after the interval sweeps again and reclaims records for deleted and UID-replaced sets while preserving other sets' (and other namespaces' same-named sets') records.

While a sweep is in progress (mutex held), another worker's prune call returns promptly without blocking and without advancing the sweep clock. This is the property that distinguishes TryLock from a plain Lock; the PR's own TestPruneInstanceHealthConcurrent cannot tell them apart.

Deferring the sweep is correctness-safe: within the throttle window (no sweep at all), a same-name recreated set inherits neither the old set's unhealthy window (observeInstanceHealth reclaims old-UID entries and starts a fresh one) nor the old rollback signal (readers self-invalidate on setUID mismatch).

benchmarks.note: Evidence, not red/green gates. Run: go test -mod=vendor ./pkg/reconciler/roleinstanceset/statefulmode/ -run '^$' -bench 'BenchmarkV501|BenchmarkPruneInstanceHealth' -benchmem -benchtime=200ms -count=1
covers: hot-path prune cost is O(1) at any map size (15ns, 0 allocs) — PR's claimed win, reproduced
due-sweep cost ~O(N) (9.6us/1.19ms at 100/10k entries) — now at most once per minute
F2 evidence: observeInstanceHealth still Ranges the global map per reconcile (116ns/856ns/214us at 0/100/10k other-set entries) — pre-existing, untouched by this PR

liveNote: L3 (live cluster) intentionally skipped per the debate-round instructions (unit + integration only). No integration (envtest) layer either: the change is pure in-memory control flow around two package-level sync.Maps plus lister reads that a cache.Indexer fake exercises fully; a real API server adds no signal for this contract. The PR's own e2e/CI coverage is unaffected by an in-memory cadence change.
